signature.name: Ljubljana Castle
signature.detail: The hilltop castle is the city's defining sight, with views over the old town and river. Walk up from the old town or take the funicular; go early morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Triple Bridge
signature.detail: This trio of bridges by Jože Plečnik links the old town with the modern centre and is the city's most photographed spot. It is free and open at all hours, so visit at dusk when the riverside cafés light up.

signature.name: Prešeren Square
signature.detail: The main square is the heart of the old town, framed by the Franciscan church and the Triple Bridge. It is a natural starting point for a walking tour; mornings are calmest.

signature.name: St. Nicholas Cathedral
signature.detail: The city's main cathedral is known for its ornate baroque interior and bronze doors. It is free to enter outside service times; dress modestly and keep quiet during mass.

signature.name: Tivoli Park
signature.detail: Ljubljana's largest park offers wooded paths and a formal promenade leading up to the castle hill. It is free and ideal for a morning walk; enter from Prešeren Square via the Jakopič promenade.

signature.name: Metelkova Mesto
signature.detail: This former barracks turned autonomous art and culture zone is covered in murals and street art. Visit in daylight for photos and check what is on in the evening; it is a short walk from the centre.

signature.name: National Museum of Slovenia
signature.detail: The country's main museum holds archaeology and history collections, including the famous Ljubljana Marshes wheel. Check opening days before you go and allow a couple of hours.

transport: City bus about $1.50 a ride; centre is very walkable
